Admissions
The David and Judi Proctor Department of Mathematics at the University of Oklahoma is now accepting applications for Fall 2027. For more information, please see below.
Application Deadline
For Fall 2027 admissions, applications submitted by January 15, 2027 will be given full consideration. After
this date, the graduate committee will review new applications through April or
until all positions are filled.
Acceptance Deadline
Like most serious graduate programs, OU is a signer of the April 15 Resolution.
Accordingly, the deadline for accepting an offer from us cannot occur before
April 15. For more information, and to see which universities are signatories
of this agreement, see
April 15 Resolution.
How to apply
To apply to our MA/PhD program or our MS program, complete an application here.
Entrance requirements for our programs may be found here.
A limited number of waivers to the application fee are available. The application for a fee waiver and more information can be found here. Be aware that fee waivers are decided after the January 15th deadline; students who apply for the fee waiver by January 15th will be given an opportunity to apply after the deadline (regardless whether they are awarded a fee waiver).
Required Application Materials
Electronic application
Statement of interest
Resume/CV
GRE scores are not required this year. However, we strongly encourage
applicants to submit GRE scores so that we are better able to evaluate their
application.
Three letters of recommendation
These should be from people familiar with your work in mathematics. Please
encourage your letter writers to read our advice for letter writers.
Transcripts
These should be copies of your recent, official transcript.
International students only:
Proof of English proficiency, which may be one of the following.
Duolingo English Test (DET) score of at least 130.
TOEFL (iBT) score of at least 79.
IELTS (Academic) score of at least 6.
PTE Academic score of at least 60.
Citizenship or a Bachelor's degree from an English-speaking country on this list.
Other exemption options are listed here.
Financial support documentation will be need be submitted in the final
application to OU, but not to the initial application to the Math Department.
For more details, see here.
For all other Graduate College requirements for international students, see
here.
All applicants will automatically be considered for a Graduate Teaching Assistantship.
Note, if you feel that your college experience, and hence your application, has
been affected by the covid pandemic, you should make a short section in the
statement of interest to address this point.
Useful suggestions
When you fill out your online application form, choose either the MS program
(if you are interested in a terminal Master's degree), the MA program if you're
interested in a PhD in mathematics and do not have a masters degree in
mathematics, or the PhD program if you're interested in a PhD in mathematics
and have a masters degree in mathematics.
Please note that we can not support international MS students with
assistantships.
Being timely, thorough and complete will increase your application's chances of
acceptance.
In particular, make sure your references submit their letters of recommendation
by the January 15 deadline.
What comes next?
After January 15, the Mathematics Department's Graduate Committee will review
all complete applications. You will be notified of the department's decision
via e-mail. As long as you have not received any notification, it means that no
decision has been made.
OU is a signer of the Council of Graduate School's April 15 Resolution. This
means that, in case we make you an offer, we will not require your response
before April 15.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I get an application fee waiver?
Yes! You may read more about our waiver and apply on https://www.mathjobs.org/jobs/list/29162. Be aware that you may not receive a decision on your waiver until after the January 15th deadline. As long as you apply for a waiver by January 15th, you will count as having “met the deadline” for the official application as well.
Will you review my application materials before I submit my application?
No.
We do not review applications, or application materials, outside the normal
application process. Please submit your application online and we will review
it during the spring admissions season.
Do I need to secure the support of a faculty member before applying?
No. Students are admitted to the program overall. There is no need to specify a potential advisor.
Are assistantships reserved for PhD students only?
No.
For the MA/PhD program, all successful applicants will be offered a teaching
assistantship. For the MS program, we offer assistantships for domestic
students, but not international.
Is the stipend that comes with an assistantship enough to cover all living expenses?
Yes, the stipend is designed to cover all living expenses under normal circumstances. You will also receive a tuition waiver and basic health insurance. See the tab "Financial Support" at the left for more information.
Is there a minimum GPA?
No.
All GPA's will be considered, but generally successful applicants possess a 3.0
cumulative GPA from their undergraduate and/or graduate work. For
international students, this can be difficult to compute/convert and so we
recommend you submit an application and let us convert the GPA as we are
reviewing applications.
Is there a minimum GRE score?
No. (The GRE is currently not required.)
I only took the general GRE, not the GRE subject test. Is this a
disadvantage?
No.
The GRE subject test is not required. (The general GRE is currently not required either.)
I am unable to submit a complete application by January 15. Will I still be
considered?
Yes.
Your application will be reviewed as soon as it is complete. However, please
make an effort to submit all your materials as soon as possible.
The January 15th deadline is approaching/has passed, and I still haven't heard back about my fee waiver. Should I be worried?
There is nothing to worry about, and there is no need to complete the official application yet. As long as you apply for a waiver by January 15th, you will count as having “met the deadline” for the official application. When you receive a decision on your waiver application (regardless of whether you get a waiver or not), you will be given a window of time in which to complete the official application.
Do you admit students for the spring semester?
No,
the starting date for all students will be in the fall semester.
I have an undergraduate degree from a foreign institution and am not sure
whether this makes me eligible to apply.
This is almost never a problem. If you are worried, you are welcome to
contact the Office of Graduate Admissions in the Graduate College and they will
be able to help you determine your eligibility.
Where can I learn more about the fees?
Since only tuition is covered with your offer from us, knowing the fees is
essential. You can learn more about the amount and how to pay fees by
following these two links.
https://www.ou.edu/bursar/tuition_fees/calculator
https://www.ou.edu/bursar/bill_pay/payment_plans
In the first link, be sure to select "Qualifying Graduate Assistant" at the top, use 9 hours for each semester, and select "College of
Arts and Sciences (Graduate)".
